definition: The desert world explored by the declared 4e Dark Sun Campaign Setting witness.
cultural_caution: A fictional setting world, not a character node or an automatic home for all core-D&D material.

supports: The product synopsis identifies Athas as the setting world.

definition: The ruling category named in the 4e product synopsis for Athas.
cultural_caution: A source-specific political/magical category. No individual sorcerer-king is created without a separate claim-level record, and no real-world political analogy is asserted.

supports: The official synopsis calls Athas a world ruled by sorcerer-kings.

definition: A power tradition identified by Wizards as common in Athas, distinct from magic in the cited rules discussion.
cultural_caution: A setting/rules concept, not an individual ability claim or a universal property of every Athasian character.

citations.locator: Psionics and the Mystic, Take 2, p. 2, 'Psionics and Settings'
supports: Wizards identifies Athas in Dark Sun as a setting where psionics is common and distinguishes psionics from magic.

definition: Wizards' broad description of magic's environmental harm in Athas; it is retained without asserting unexposed defiler/preserver mechanics.
cultural_caution: Do not substitute generic environmental magic, infer detailed rule effects, or turn ecological collapse into aesthetic scenery divorced from the setting's coercion and survival themes.

citations.locator: Psionics and the Mystic, Take 2, p. 2, 'Psionics and Settings'
supports: The Wizards document calls magic in Athas an ecological scourge.

definition: The explicitly named 4e game-support areas in the Dark Sun Campaign Setting synopsis.
cultural_caution: These are edition-specific play procedures, not universal setting facts or a basis for importing a 4e mechanical profile into other editions.

supports: The official synopsis names rules/advice for survival challenges, arena encounters, and desert terrain.
